title: Syntax suffix under a leading bit
statement: For a state $q\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ and a bit string $x$, define the suffix condition as follows: in state $0$, $x$ encodes a CNF formula; in state $1$, it is a clause encoding followed by a formula encoding; in state $2$, it has the form $1^v0b$ followed by a clause encoding and a formula encoding, for some $v\in\mathbb N$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$; in state $3$, it is a bit followed by a clause encoding and a formula encoding; in state $4$, it is empty; and in state $5$, the condition is false. For every such state $q$, bit $b$, and finite bit string $x$, the condition holds for $b$ followed by $x$ exactly when it holds for $x$ in the state reached from $q$ by the transition rule: on input $1$, states $0,1,2,3$ go respectively to $1,2,2,1$; on input $0$, they go respectively to $4,0,3,1$; either input from states $4$ or $5$ leads to $5$.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is one of the six states $0,1,2,3,4,5$
